item.title: Trump Demands Rate Cut After Jobs Report
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Larry Sabato, founder and director of the University of Virginia Center for Politics, says next week's Republican midterm convention, headlined by President Trump, is unlikely to reshape the dynamics of competitive House races. Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, discusses legislation he is proposing with Sen. Bernie Sanders that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence, temporarily pause advanced AI development, and establish a new federal AI regulator. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Casar: US Needs to Put the Brakes on Advanced AI
item.description: Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, discusses legislation he is proposing with Sen. Bernie Sanders that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence, temporarily pause advanced AI development, and establish a new federal AI regulator. Casar says companies should be barred from pursuing artificial superintelligence, while research on AI that is safe and beneficial could continue. He also discusses divisions among House Democrats and the role of the Progressive Caucus if Democrats win control of the chamber. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sabato: RNC Convention Unlikely to Move Midterm Needle
item.description: Larry Sabato, founder and director of the University of Virginia Center for Politics, says next week's Republican midterm convention, headlined by President Trump, is unlikely to reshape the dynamics of competitive House races. He also discusses the legal fight over Missouri's congressional map and the dispute over mail ballots in North Carolina. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Judge Blocks Mail Ballot Change as Supreme Court Weighs Case
item.description: A federal judge has blocked the Postal Service from enforcing new limits on mail-in voting through the Nov. 3 midterm elections, extending a short-term pause as North Carolina began sending ballots on Friday and the US Justice Department was urging the Supreme Court to intervene.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman and Brian Dowling

item.title: Travel, Retail, US Open: Labor Day Edition | Bloomberg Money 9/4/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: The Points Guy Founder Brian Kelly and Telsey Advisory Group CEO & Chief Research Officer Dana Telsey. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Strong Payrolls Fuel Fed Hike Bets | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/4/2026
item.description: A stronger-than-anticipated increase in US jobs drove stocks and short-dated bonds lower, with traders boosting their bets the Federal Reserve will raise rates this month. While analysts expect the September Fed decision will hinge on next week’s inflation data, swap contracts priced in an over 50% chance of a hike. Anna Wong, Chief US Economist at Bloomberg Economics, and Constance Hunter, Chief Economist and Head of Research at Economist Enterprise, join to discuss. Plus, Bloomberg News White House & Washington Correspondent Jeff Mason discusses President Trump's reaction to the payrolls report and his announcement that he will allow ranchers to process their own beef. Finally, Poonam Goyal, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Analyst for E-Commerce and Retail, breaks down Lululemon's weaker-than-expected earnings report, with shares of the athleisure company falling close to 19% to their lowest level since May 2018. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says US Will Host State Dinner for China's Xi
item.description: The US will hold a formal state dinner in honor of President Xi Jinping when the Chinese leader visits Washington later this month, President Donald Trump said. Trump spoke to reporters in the Oval Office on Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Calls Iran Conflict ‘Small Potatoes,’ Plays Down War
item.description: President Donald Trump called the war in Iran “small potatoes,” the latest comment from a top US leader downplaying the scope of a conflict that has lasted more than six months.

item.title: Key Takeaways From the US August Jobs Report
item.description: US nonfarm payrolls increased 162,000 last month and the unemployment rate remained at 4.1%, with the August increase topping all estimates in a Bloomberg survey. Anna Wong, chief US economist with Bloomberg Economics, says the economy may not be as strong as it seems. Here are her key takeaways. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Backs Beef Origin Labels, Boosts Rancher Processing
item.description: President Donald Trump moved to require country-of-origin labeling on foreign beef, in the latest effort to appease ranchers angered by the White House’s plan to boost foreign imports.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Ilena Peng

item.title: Trump’s Big Venezuela Deal Leaves US Oil Industry Blindsided
item.description: President Donald Trump has boasted that his sweeping oil accord with Venezuela — effectively giving the US control over much of the nation’s crude wealth — is possibly “the greatest deal ever made.”
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Kevin Crowley and David Wethe

item.title: Trump Demands Fed Lower Rates, Reviving Pressure Campaign

item.title: US Envoys to Make Ukraine Peace Push With Russia Pessimistic
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to arrive in Moscow on Saturday with a proposal to end the years-long conflict with Ukraine, though Russia expressed pessimism about the prospects of the trip resulting in any sort of deal.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: North Carolina Mailing Ballots Friday as Legal Battle Rages
item.description: North Carolina began sending out mail-in ballots on Friday, a key milestone as the US Supreme Court weighs whether to intervene in a legal fight that could help determine control of Congress after the November election.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson
